Subject: POC acceptance criteria, SLOs, and evaluation onboarding

Ava / Samir —

Thanks again for taking time to run through the feasibility call today. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the proposed acceptance criteria and next steps for the 3-week POC so we have alignment before we kick off. High-level asks below; I attached a short checklist you can drop into your tracker.

Summary of proposed POC scope:
- Workload: chat + retrieval augmentation for customer support intents (approx. ~1.2k tokens/session average)
- Duration: 3 weeks (pilot traffic ramp in week 1, steady-state eval weeks 2–3)
- Goals: validate latency and cost under representative load, measure response quality vs. existing baseline, and verify security controls for tokens/logs retention

Proposed acceptance criteria (must pass all):
1) P95 latency end-to-end (user request to first token): <= 250 ms for 95% of traffic during steady state
2) Sustained throughput: support 120 concurrent sessions with 8 requests/min average per session without queueing beyond 100 ms
3) Cost/token: average inference cost <= $0.0009/token at steady-state batching config (Redwood estimate)
4) Quality: automated eval on 3 priority intent prompts must be >= 4.2/5 (precision and helpfulness) and no major hallucination failures in spot-check set
5) Security/compliance: no user PII persist in logs; JSON-based sample retention policy applied; KMS key configured for customer workspace

Ownership and deliverables:
- Veridian: provide sample traffic CSV, priority intent prompt set, and any rate-limit constraints (owner: Ava)
- Redwood: provide config for batching/quant profiles, sample-run scripts, and daily test harness (owner: Jordan)
- CS/Onboarding: weekly check-ins and final review (owner: Monica)

Immediate next steps:
- You to share sample-traffic-spec and priority intents by EOD 2026-11-30
- We will provision a sandbox instance and share onboarding docs + runbook by 2026-12-01
- Kickoff meeting to schedule after we confirm traffic upload (suggest Tue 2026-12-01 10am PST)

Attaching: POC-Acceptance-Checklist.xlsx and sample-traffic-spec.json

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

— Jordan

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear recap. This is close to what we discussed. A couple of clarifying points from our side:
- Latency: our users are in US East; would the 250 ms P95 target be measured from our East region or is that global? We need regional expectations in the checklist.
- Throughput: instead of concurrency, can we express as sustained QPS? Our infra team prefers that. For our expected peak, think ~160 QPS sustained during business hours.
- Cost: the $/token estimate looks reasonable; we'd like a sensitivity table for +/-20% token sizes and batching window to see how that moves the cost.

We will upload the sample traffic and priority intents by EOD Monday (2026-11-30). Security will loop in a short questionnaire; I’ve CC’d Samir (security) and they may ask for evidence of encryption-at-rest for trial data.
